'''Patrick Fitzgerald O'Bryant''' (born June 20, 1986) is an American-Central African former professional [[basketball]] player. The {{Cvt|7|ft|cm|0}}, {{cvt|250|lb|kg st}} [[Center (basketball)|center]] was selected out of [[Bradley University]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the 9th overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]]. He has been a member of the NBA's Warriors, [[Boston Celtics]], and [[Toronto Raptors]], and has also played in the [[NBA Development League]], and overseas in Europe and Latin America.

==College==
O'Bryant attended [[Bradley University]] for two years and led the [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Braves]] to the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Sweet Sixteen]] of the [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2006 NCAA tournament]] before losing to [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|University of Memphis]]. His breakout performance against traditional powerhouses [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]]<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/ncaatourney06/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=2379926 These five have helped shake up the bracket - Men's College Basketball - ESPN]</ref> at the tournament caught the eyes of NBA scouts. But in late 2005, O'Bryant, along with another student, was suspended for 8 games by the NCAA for receiving improper payments for work claimed he had undertaken in the summer, but had not actually done. All up he was paid $1,100 on a weekly basis, regardless of whether he showed up to work or not.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2234121 NCAA suspends Bradley basketball players - Men's College Basketball - ESPN]</ref> On April 22, 2006, O'Bryant declared for the [[2006 NBA draft|NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent, making him eligible to return to college.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2006/news/story?id=2420355 Bradley's O'Bryant to enter draft, without agent - NBA - ESPN]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2006/news/story?id=2418964 O'Bryant declares for draft, doesn't hire agent - NBA - ESPN]</ref> However, O'Bryant made his declaration official the following month when he hired Andy Miller as his agent.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2006/news/story?id=2450953 O'Bryant hires agent, commits to entering NBA draft - NBA - ESPN]</ref>

==Professional career==

===Golden State Warriors===
On June 28, 2006, O'Bryant was selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the 9th overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]]. On September 6, he was diagnosed with a fracture in his right foot. He was placed in an immobilizing boot on the injured foot and missed six weeks of training camp. He played sparingly in the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]].

O'Bryant became the first [[NBA]] [[NBA draft lottery|lottery pick]] to be sent down to the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League|D-League]] on December 30, 2006. On February 19, 2007, he was recalled from the Jam. [[Golden State Warriors|Warriors]] head coach [[Don Nelson]] had critical words for him: "I told him if he goes down to the D-League and isn't a dominant player, there should be red flags all over the place, and he should be the first to notice. He's not only not dominating, he's not playing very well. He's a long-term project. I really liked him the first week of training camp, but I assumed there would be great progress. [...] He hasn't gotten better one bit."<ref>{{cite news |first=Geoff |last=Lepper |title=Rookie stays in D-League |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4176/is_20070125/ai_n17165586 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081019123346/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4176/is_20070125/ai_n17165586 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=October 19, 2008 |work=[[The Oakland Tribune|Oakland Tribune]]|date=January 25, 2007 |access-date=2007-12-29}}</ref>

Prior to the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], the [[Golden State Warriors|Warriors]] declined to pick up his third-year option, which made him an [[unrestricted free agent]] at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Warriors Decline To Exercise Third-Year Option On Contract Of Patrick O'Bryant |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/Warriors_Decline_OBryant_Option.html |work=NBA.com |date=November 1, 2007 |access-date=2007-12-29}}</ref> On March 10, 2008, he was reassigned to the Bakersfield Jam; however, he was later recalled and rejoined the Warriors for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/twolves-summer-league-central-2010|title=#Twolves Summer League Central 2010|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref>

===Boston Celtics===
On July 11, 2008, O'Bryant signed a two-year, $3.12 million contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref name=globe>Marc J. Spears, [http://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2008/07/12/celtics_get_their_big/ Celtics get their 'big'], ''[[The Boston Globe]]'', July 12, 2008.</ref> He had an impressive workout with the team a week earlier and was expected to be the backup [[Center (basketball)|center]] for [[Kendrick Perkins]].<ref name=globe/>

===Toronto Raptors===
On February 19, 2009, O'Bryant was traded by Boston to the Toronto Raptors in a 3-team deal with [[Will Solomon]] going to the [[Sacramento Kings]], and a heavily protected future second-round pick going to the Celtics.<ref name="O'Bryant Raptors">{{cite web
|url = https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press021909-obryant-trade.html
|title = Celtics Trade O'Bryant
|publisher = Celtics.com
|access-date = 2020-08-24}}</ref>

===China===
In September, 2010, O'Bryant signed a contract with [[Fujian Xunxing]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]],<ref name="Former BU center in China">{{cite web
 |url        = http://www.bradleyhoops.com/news/x161453546/Former-BU-center-in-China
 |title      = Former BU center in China
 |publisher  = Peoria Journal-Star
 |access-date = 2010-10-06
}}{{dead link|date=March 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> but was later released because of poor performances in pre-season, as well as a reported lack of effort in practice.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.niubball.com/2010/12/fujian-to-release-patrick-obryant-shanxi-adds-jamal-sampson/ |title=Fujian to release Patrick O’Bryant, Shanxi adds Jamal Sampson |access-date=December 9, 2010 |archive-date=March 14, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314155105/http://www.niubball.com/2010/12/fujian-to-release-patrick-obryant-shanxi-adds-jamal-sampson/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Return to the NBA D-League===
On January 10, 2011, O'Bryant joined the [[Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bakersfield.com/news/sports/local/x864760057/Jam-acquires-OBryant-sends-him-to-Bighorns-for-draft-pick |title=Jam acquires O'Bryant, sends him to Bighorns for draft pick |access-date=January 13, 2011 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181855/http://www.bakersfield.com/news/sports/local/x864760057/Jam-acquires-OBryant-sends-him-to-Bighorns-for-draft-pick |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Europe===
In August 2011 he signed with [[Kavala B.C.]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/greece/30555/kavala_lands_former_nba_player_patrick_o_bryant.html |title=Kavala lands former NBA player Patrick O'Bryant |access-date=2011-08-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110919195532/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/greece/30555/kavala_lands_former_nba_player_patrick_o_bryant.html |archive-date=2011-09-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Puerto Rico===
In February 2012 he signed with the [[Indios de Mayagüez]] of Puerto Rico.<ref>[https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/basketball.aspx?NewsID=261923 Indios sign OBryant]{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

===Return to Reno and Lietuvos Rytas===
On January 16, 2013, O'Bryant was reacquired by the Reno Bighorns.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/bighorns_acquire_patrick_obry_2013_01_16.html |title=BIGHORNS ACQUIRE PATRICK O'BRYANT |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2013-01-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160123102331/http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/bighorns_acquire_patrick_obry_2013_01_16.html |archive-date=2016-01-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was bought out of his contract on January 30. He then joined [[BC Rytas|Lietuvos rytas]]. Despite being signed as one of the team's main centers, his playing time decreased over the following months. O'Bryant was released on May 6, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/lithuania/55247/patrick-o-bryant-lietuvos-rytas-part-ways.html |title=Patrick O'Bryant, Lietuvos Rytas part ways |access-date=2013-05-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130513185345/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/lithuania/55247/patrick-o-bryant-lietuvos-rytas-part-ways.html |archive-date=2013-05-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Charlotte Bobcats===
In September 2013, O'Bryant signed with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14382 |title=Bobcats add Troy Daniels, Abdul Gaddy, Patrick O'Bryant to training camp |access-date=2013-10-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131001084049/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14382 |archive-date=2013-10-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was waived on October 23.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14617 |title=Charlotte Bobcats waive Patrick O'Bryant |access-date=2013-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029190440/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14617 |archive-date=2013-10-29 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Taiwan===
In November 2013, O'Bryant signed with [[Taiwan Beer (basketball)|Taiwan Beer]] of the [[Super Basketball League]].
On April 24, 2016, O'Bryant won the Final's MVP award while playing for Taiwan Beer.

===The BIG3 League===
On May 5, 2018, O'Bryant signed on to play in the [[BIG3]] League.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2018/3/5/17081944/2018-nba-golden-state-warriors-center-patrick-obryant-joins-big3-ice-cube|title = Former Warrior Patrick O'Bryant joins the Big3|date = 5 March 2018}}</ref> He also coaches in Las Vegas with the private coaching service, [[CoachUp]].<ref>[http://www.coachup.com/coaches/patricko-8 www.coachup.com/coaches/patricko-8]</ref>

===London Lightning===
On October 27, 2018, O'Bryant signed with the [[London Lightning]] of the [[National Basketball League of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usbasket.com/NBLCanada/news/552351/Former-players:-Patrick-O'Bryant-is-a-newcomer-at-London-Lightning|title = US Basketball News, Scores, Stats, Analysis, Standings}}</ref>

==National team career==
O'Bryant holds a [[Central African Republic|Central African]] passport, and has played with the senior [[Central African Republic men's national basketball team|Central African national team]] at the [[AfroBasket 2013]] tournament, helping the team reach the playoff stage.

==Playing style==
O'Bryant was a late bloomer who was not heavily recruited out of high school. He plays the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position and is known for his [[shot-blocking]] ability, as he led the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] in blocks for two straight years, and is also a solid rebounder. He has a 7'6" wingspan. His offensive game also features a [[Hook shot|skyhook]].
